note: Full-website pass (landing -> user panel) for redundancy + content-truth, fused with the 9-axis improvement plan. Every premise pre-verified against live code (S175). The dominant theme: 233 sessions optimized the telemetry/gate layer to a near-ceiling SIL while several VISITOR-FACING truths drifted (wrong auth return domain, sealed:7, gold-vs-blue tier theme, 393 days). The highest-leverage work is (a) one content-truth pass, (b) gate the drift CLASS so it can't recur, (c) reduce per-session agent token cost via diff-scoped gates, (d) deepen the AI + gamification surfaces that are currently skin-deep.

items.title: Oracle: deploy-time prebaked answer corpus + agent-callable Answer API (real RAG, zero runtime cost)
items.why: The Oracle (assets/ignis-answer-engine.js answer()) is pure client-side keyword hay-scoring with a templated 'IGNIS read:' wrapper — zero synthesis. Meanwhile the site brands itself dual-audience (CANON-048) but offers AI crawlers no synthesized, citable answers. Prebaking the top ~50 real queries (from api/oracle-queries.json) into a committed oracle/answers/<slug>.json via ONE batched Claude (Haiku) call per deploy gives genuine prose answers with zero per-session/runtime API cost (CANON-029), and an agent-discoverable GET endpoint makes VaultSpark the GEO/AEO source for questions about its own portfolio.
items.recipe: 1) scripts/build-oracle-answers.mjs: read api/oracle-queries.json top-N, retrieve top-3 doc snippets per query from public-intelligence.json, one batched Haiku call -> committed oracle/answers/index.json (honest, deploy-time, cached). 2) Oracle UI: serve prose answer from the committed JSON on match, fall back to current keyword engine. 3) Advertise GET /oracle/answers/index.json in agents.json actions[]. 4) Add JSON-LD QAPage to oracle/index.html.

L1.recipe: Hand-write 8 canonical Q&A pairs (pricing, what-is-VaultSpark, which-game, how-to-join) into oracle/answers/index.json; serve from there before the keyword engine.

L2.recipe: build-oracle-answers.mjs with batched Haiku call over top-30 queries, committed JSON, keyword fallback, self-test + freshness gate.

L3.recipe: Full corpus prebake + agent Answer API in agents.json + JSON-LD QAPage + per-deploy regen wired into the build, with a daily KV cache on the Worker for any live 'explain' expansions.

items.title: Self-contradiction sentinel — gate cross-feed truth drift before it ships
items.why: This audit found four live visitor-facing contradictions (sealed:7, gold-vs-blue tier theme, 393 days, press vaulted count) that 233 sessions of gates never caught because each gate checks one surface in isolation. The recurring CLASS is cross-surface drift: api/public-status.json, api/public-intelligence.json, membership pages, and the homepage SSR snapshot disagree. A single sentinel that diffs shared facts (counts, status labels, vocab, theme names, launch date) across all public surfaces and BLOCKS build:check on contradiction kills the entire class — far higher leverage than fixing each instance by hand. CANON-031 (no lying surfaces).
items.recipe: 1) scripts/check-content-coherence.mjs: load the public feeds + key marketing HTML, assert invariants (vaulted count == feed; theme-name strings match across membership/membership-value; no retired vocab 'sealed/SEALED'; days-since-launch derives from launch date; game status label == feed status). 2) Self-test with the 4 known-bad fixtures. 3) Wire into check-proof-surface.mjs (no new build:check &&-segment — respects the 8191 cmd.exe ceiling).

L1.recipe: Grep gate: fail build:check if 'sealed'/'SEALED' or a hardcoded days-since-launch integer appears in any public HTML/JSON.

L2.recipe: Full cross-feed invariant checker (counts/labels/vocab/theme-names/launch) wired into check-proof-surface, 6+ self-tests, control-proven.

L3.recipe: Add a nightly Action that posts a coherence digest to nervous-system + opens an issue on drift, so even non-build content edits are caught within 24h.

items.title: P0: fix wrong Obelisk auth return domain (vaultspark.studio -> vaultsparkstudios.com)
items.why: login.html line 16 sets data-obelisk-return='https://vaultspark.studio/auth/callback' — the WRONG domain (canonical is vaultsparkstudios.com). Every Obelisk sign-in attempt returns to a domain the site does not serve, dead-ending the login. The byte-identical duplicate at obelisk-passport/login.html carries the same bug. This is the single most impactful cheap fix in the audit: a broken primary auth entry point on a live site. (The deeper Obelisk<->Supabase reconciliation is escalated separately — auth-flow change.)
items.recipe: 1) Edit login.html + auth callback config: return -> https://vaultsparkstudios.com/auth/callback. 2) Delete obelisk-passport/{login,callback}.html (verified byte-identical dupes) OR redirect them. 3) Add a gate asserting obelisk-return host == canonical host.

L1.recipe: One-line domain fix in login.html + delete the obelisk-passport dupes.

L2.recipe: Domain fix + dupe removal + a check-auth-config gate pinning the return host to the canonical domain.

L3.recipe: Above + a Playwright smoke that drives /login and asserts the return URL host is canonical.

items.title: agents.json feed + action catalog — make the ~48 public api/*.json discoverable to AI
items.why: agents.json currently advertises only status-proof + citation, so the ~48 public api/*.json feeds (public-intelligence, nervous-system, oracle-insights, velocity-series, ...) are undiscoverable to the AI agents the site claims to serve (CANON-048). A generated feeds[]/actions[] catalog with each feed's schema + freshness turns the site from 'has feeds' into 'navigable by agents' — and it can be derived, not hand-listed, so it never drifts.
items.recipe: 1) scripts/build-agents-feed-catalog.mjs: enumerate git-tracked api/*.json, emit {path, title, schemaHint, generatedAt} into agents.json feeds[]. 2) Add actions[] for the Oracle Answer API (pairs with oracle-prebake). 3) Link .well-known/entity-graph.json from JSON-LD sameAs. 4) --check determinism gate.

L1.recipe: Hand-add the 8 most useful feeds to agents.json feeds[].

L2.recipe: Generated catalog over all tracked api/*.json with schema hints + freshness, --check gated.

L3.recipe: Above + machine-readable action verbs + entity-graph sameAs links + an llms.txt section indexing the feeds.

items.title: Diff-scoped gate selection — run only gates whose inputs changed (per-session token + time cut)
items.why: build:check runs ~159 sequential node spawns every session; its interleaved stdout is the single largest per-session token sink the agent re-reads at every closeout, and the cold-starts dominate wall-clock. A diff-scoped runner that maps git diff --name-only to the gates covering those files, and skips untouched gate CLASSES locally (full sweep stays in CI), cuts both agent token consumption and dev-loop time with zero coverage loss. This directly serves the explicit ask: reduce project token/API consumption without sacrificing quality.
items.recipe: 1) scripts/gate-scope.mjs: a manifest mapping each check-*.mjs to its input globs. 2) npm run check:scoped reads git diff --name-only and runs only matching gates + always-on invariants. 3) CI keeps the full build:check. 4) Print a one-line 'skipped N untouched gate classes' summary instead of 159 logs.

L1.recipe: Add npm run check:fast that runs the ~12 highest-signal gates only, for the inner dev loop.

L2.recipe: Gate->input-glob manifest + diff-scoped runner; full sweep stays in CI; quiet summary output.

L3.recipe: Pair with the in-process orchestrator so scoped runs execute in one node process — ~10x faster and minimal agent-watched stdout.

items.title: Agent-aware edge UA policy — stop blocking the HTTP clients AI agents use
items.why: cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js BLOCKED_UA_PATTERNS hard-blocks curl, wget, python-requests, go-http-client, and libwww-perl alongside genuine attack tools (sqlmap, nuclei, nmap). Those five are exactly the default HTTP libraries legitimate AI agents and API clients use — a direct contradiction of the site's CANON-048 'built for AI agents' promise. Keep blocking the scanner toolset; let generic HTTP clients read public content (optionally rate-limited), so the dual-audience claim is real at the edge, not just in the marketing copy.
items.recipe: 1) Split BLOCKED_UA_PATTERNS into SCANNER_TOOLS (keep blocking) and GENERIC_HTTP (curl/wget/requests/go-http/libwww). 2) Allow GENERIC_HTTP on public GET read paths; keep them rate-limited via the existing RATE_LIMIT KV. 3) Still block them on GATED_PATH_PATTERNS + write methods. 4) Deploy Worker; note in DECISIONS.

L1.recipe: Remove curl/wget/requests/go-http/libwww from BLOCKED_UA_PATTERNS (keep the scanner tools); deploy.

L2.recipe: Path-scoped policy: generic clients allowed on public reads + rate-limited, blocked on gated/write; deploy + DECISIONS note.

L3.recipe: Add a documented agent-access lane (advertised in agents.json) with a soft token-bucket and a 200 'agent welcome' header on api/* reads.

items.title: Live 'what's your membership worth' calculator on /membership-value/
items.why: membership-value/ currently states a static '~$32-60/mo' range and (worse) contradicts the membership page on the tier theme color. Replace the static range with an interactive calculator: the visitor checks the games/tools they would actually use and sees a personalized $/mo value vs the $4.99 price — a concrete, self-computed reason to convert, and a far stronger anchor than a hand-waved range. Doubles as the place to source tier facts from one JSON (kills the gold-vs-blue drift at the root).
items.recipe: 1) api/membership-tiers.json as the single source of tier facts + per-perk notional value. 2) membership-value calculator: checkbox list of perks -> live summed $/mo vs price, with a 'this is X.Xx the price' headline. 3) emitUx('value-calc:compute') for funnel telemetry. 4) Render the static tier lists on membership + join from the same JSON.

L1.recipe: Fix the gold->blue theme contradiction + replace the static range with a single derived 'members use ~$X/mo of value' line from a tiers JSON.

L2.recipe: Interactive perk-picker calculator with personalized $/mo and funnel telemetry.

L3.recipe: Calculator + signed-in personalization (pull the member's actual usage) + a shareable 'my value' card via the OG rasterizer.

items.title: Status-aware game cards — auto-flip CTA from the live feed (kills the Demo-vs-Live drift class)
items.why: Game catalog cards and detail pages hardcode status + CTA (Play / Get Return Notice / Notify), which is the exact source of the recurring 'Demo Coming Soon over a working Play link' drift (the S197 lesson). Deriving each card's status label AND CTA from api/public-intelligence.json at build/runtime means a re-sparked or vaulted game updates everywhere from one feed edit — the drift class can't recur.
items.recipe: 1) Build-time inject status+CTA into games/index.html cards + games/<slug> hero from public-intelligence.json. 2) A runtime micro-hydrate for live status. 3) check-game-playability-coherence already exists — extend it to assert card CTA == feed status. 4) Remove the hardcoded status strings.

L1.recipe: Fix the currently-drifted cards by hand + tighten check-game-playability-coherence to compare CTA target against status.

L2.recipe: Build-time derive status+CTA for all game cards/heroes from the feed; remove hardcoded strings.

L3.recipe: Runtime status hydrate + a 'status changed' nervous-system event so the homepage hero and catalog never disagree.

items.title: Live 'X Vault Points to next tier' delta chip on /ranks/ and member profile
items.why: The rank ladder (8 tiers, 249 -> 99,999 Vault Points) is real but presented read-only — a flat table with no pull. Injecting 'You are X Vault Points from {next tier}' from the member's Supabase point balance onto ranks/ and the member profile converts a static ladder into a progress mechanic with a concrete next goal — the single highest-ROI gamification change because the data and tiers already exist.
items.recipe: 1) vault-member/portal reads point balance (already does for the dashboard). 2) On ranks/ + member profile, compute next-tier threshold - balance and render a progress bar + delta chip. 3) emitUx('rank:next-delta-view'). 4) Logged-out sees the generic ladder (no leak).

L1.recipe: Static 'next tier needs N points' annotations on each ranks/ row.

L2.recipe: Live personalized delta chip + progress bar from the member's real balance, signed-in only.

L3.recipe: Add momentum ('+N this week, on pace to {tier} by {date}') + a notify-me-at-next-tier hook into the existing push pipeline.

items.title: Single tier source-of-truth JSON across membership / membership-value / join (+ agent endpoint)
items.why: Tier facts (Free/$4.99/$29.99, XP, themes, Discord roles, multipliers) are written by hand on membership, membership-value, and join — and have already drifted (gold vs blue theme, differing perk lists). One api/membership-tiers.json rendered into all three at build time ends the drift permanently and makes pricing/perks AI-queryable (CANON-048). Foundational for tier-value-calculator and next-rank-delta.
items.recipe: 1) api/membership-tiers.json (price, perks[], theme, value). 2) build-membership-pages.mjs injects the perk lists into the 3 pages with --check determinism. 3) Advertise it in agents.json feeds[]. 4) Delete the hand-written drifted copies.

L1.recipe: Create the JSON + reconcile the 3 pages by hand to match it (fixes gold/blue now).

L2.recipe: Build-time render of all three pages from the JSON, --check gated.

L3.recipe: Above + a /v/ pricing endpoint and JSON-LD Offer markup so agents and rich-results read canonical pricing.

items.title: Leaderboard seasons + auto-generated shareable rank cards (referral loop)
items.why: Weekly leaderboards already exist but there is no season epoch and no reason to share a result. Adding a season reset + an auto-generated shareable rank card (reusing the existing OG SVG->PNG rasterizer) gives members a recurring 'new season, climb again' hook AND a viral artifact that feeds the existing invite/referral pipeline — closing the engagement->acquisition loop the site already has the pieces for.
items.recipe: 1) Add a season epoch to the leaderboard schema; show 'Season N · ends {date}'. 2) build-rank-card.mjs renders {handle, tier, rank, season} SVG -> PNG via sharp (already a trusted devDep). 3) share/ + member profile expose 'Share my rank'. 4) Tag shared links with the referral param.

L1.recipe: Add a visible 'Season ends {date}' countdown to the weekly board.

L2.recipe: Season epoch + shareable rank card via the OG rasterizer on the member profile.

L3.recipe: Full season lifecycle (reset, claimable end-of-season badge, season archive page) + referral attribution on shared cards.

items.title: Pathways as tracked quests — turn the 6 static explainers into progress-bearing quest lines
items.why: The 6 audience pathways are static explainer pages with no state. Turning each into a tracked multi-step quest that writes to the existing point_events table — with a visible completion bar and Vault Points on step completion — converts dead content into a retention mechanic that also drives first-session activation (a logged-in visitor has a reason to return and finish).
items.recipe: 1) Define 3-5 steps per pathway with point_event keys. 2) vault-member tracks completion; pathway pages render a per-step checklist + completion bar. 3) Award Vault Points on completion (feeds the rank delta chip). 4) emitUx('pathway:step-complete').

L1.recipe: Add a localStorage 'steps done' checklist + completion bar to one flagship pathway as a proof.

L2.recipe: Server-tracked quests writing point_events across all 6 pathways with point awards.

L3.recipe: Branching quests, pathway-complete badges on the profile, and a 'recommended next pathway' from the Oracle.

items.title: In-process gate orchestrator — collapse ~159 node spawns into one process (escape the cmd.exe cliff)
items.why: build:check is 7986/8191 chars on the Windows cmd.exe limit and spawns ~159 cold node processes per run. A single node scripts/gate.mjs that imports each check as a module (check-proof-surface.mjs already proves the spawnSync-orchestrator pattern) permanently removes the length cliff, cuts ~150 cold starts (~10x faster), and shrinks the interleaved stdout the agent ingests every closeout. Compounds with diff-scoped-gates.
items.recipe: 1) Refactor checks to export a run() returning {ok, messages}. 2) scripts/gate.mjs imports + runs them in-process, aggregates one report. 3) build:check -> node scripts/gate.mjs. 4) Keep per-gate CLI entrypoints for targeted runs.

L1.recipe: Group the 10 longest &&-segments into one spawnSync orchestrator to buy headroom under 8191 now.

L2.recipe: Full in-process import-based orchestrator with one aggregated report; build:check is a single node call.

L3.recipe: Orchestrator + parallel gate execution + per-gate timing surfaced so slow gates are visible.

items.title: Bundle the homepage's 23 footer scripts into 1-2 hashed shells (the unpulled INP/TBT lever)
items.why: index.html ships ~23 separate <script defer> files plus 3 shell bundles — ~26 files, each its own compile/eval main-thread task. This is the structural reason homepage Lighthouse is stuck at 0.76-0.78 and /games/ INP is 224ms: not one slow handler but death by a thousand small tasks. The build-shell-assets.mjs hashing pipeline already exists; concatenating the non-shell footer scripts into one hashed bundle directly attacks TBT/INP — the lever 233 sessions described but never pulled.
items.recipe: 1) Move the 23 footer <script defer> through build-shell-assets.mjs into one ambient-home shell. 2) Keep predicate-loaded feature modules behind ambient-loader.js. 3) Re-measure Lighthouse + field INP after deploy.

L1.recipe: Migrate the 8 pages still on the stale 111KB ambient.shell monolith to the split ambient-core/feature bundles (-34KB parse).

L2.recipe: Concatenate the 23 homepage footer scripts into one hashed shell via the existing pipeline; re-measure.

L3.recipe: Above + audit ambient-core (65KB) for modules that can move behind ambient-loader predicates, lowering main-thread eval sitewide.

items.title: Consolidate the intelligence surfaces — make nervous-system the canonical pane
items.why: studio-pulse, status, studio-hub, ignis, and nervous-system render largely the same derived data (public-intelligence + heartbeat + commit-map) in different skins. nervous-system is already the aggregator. Promoting it to the single 'one pane' with the others as linked sub-views (status kept as a redirect for uptime crawlers) reduces maintenance surface and visitor confusion without losing any data.
items.recipe: 1) Make nervous-system the canonical hub with tabs for CI/uptime (status) and motion (pulse). 2) status/ -> redirect/sub-view. 3) Cross-link studio-hub (portfolio) <-> studio-pulse (this repo) instead of duplicating the project list.

L1.recipe: Add reciprocal cross-links between the 5 surfaces so each points to the others (cheap coherence).

L2.recipe: nervous-system canonical pane with status/pulse as tabs; status -> redirect.

L3.recipe: Single shared loader + one design system across all intelligence surfaces; retire duplicate fetch logic.

items.title: Fix dead Oracle panels — portfolio-pulse + project-voices have no prod api/ fallback
items.why: oracle/index.html lines 415-416 fetch /ignis/output/portfolio-pulse.json and project-voices.json with only .catch(()=>null) and NO api/ fallback — those paths are gitignored and 404 on prod (the code comment even admits it), so two Oracle panels are silently dead in production. The primary ecosystem-state and velocity feeds DO have api/ fallbacks; these two were missed. Same S183 class.
items.recipe: 1) Emit public-safe api/portfolio-pulse.json + api/project-voices.json in the build (like ecosystem-state). 2) Add the api/ fallback fetch in oracle/index.html. 3) Extend check-proof-feed-generators to cover them.

L1.recipe: Hide the two panels on prod when the feed is absent (stop showing dead UI).

L2.recipe: Generate api/ copies + wire the fallback fetch + gate it.

L3.recipe: Above + fold into the agents.json feed catalog so the data is also agent-discoverable.

items.title: Consolidate the vault-*/member* directory sprawl
items.why: The member zone has redundant surfaces: obelisk-passport/{login,callback}.html are byte-identical dupes of root login/callback; vault-wall duplicates leaderboards/global + ranks; vault-treasury is a 650-byte redirect stub. Consolidating reduces the maintenance surface and the chance of the kind of drift this audit keeps finding (e.g. the dupe login carries the same wrong-domain bug).
items.recipe: 1) Delete obelisk-passport/{login,callback}.html (after the canonical login is fixed). 2) Fold vault-wall into a 'Wall' tab of leaderboards/global. 3) Collapse vault-treasury to a 301.

L1.recipe: Delete the two obelisk-passport dupes + the treasury stub redirect.

L2.recipe: Above + merge vault-wall into the global leaderboard as a view.

L3.recipe: Full member-zone IA pass: one portal entry, clearly distinct member (profile) / members (directory) / leaderboards / ranks.
